key_insight: 2D/3D perovskite band alignment is strongly controlled by surface termination and chemical composition, with interfacial polarization shifting the electrostatics and offsets.
engineering_relevance: Tuning the 2D capping layer and 3D perovskite chemistry can help engineer more stable, better-passivated solar-cell interfaces with improved electronic alignment.
method: Atomistic first-principles simulations with hybrid functionals
Calculated work function, electron affinity, and band offsets across 2D/3D layers
Compared multiple cleavages and chemical terminations for (PEA)2PbI4 / mixed-cation mixed-halide 3D interfaces
evidence_signal: The abstract reports preliminary computed results showing work functions and band offsets vary substantially with surface chemistry, with valence offsets of 0.2–0.7 eV and conduction offsets around 0.25 eV.
watch_item: Results are preliminary and simulation-based, so real-device performance may differ due to defects, disorder, and processing-dependent interfaces.
paper_title: Material chemical composition impacts on the band alignments: preliminary results on the 3D/2D perovskite interfaces
